fixes.explanation: The verse doesn't mention changing or adding to anything. Grandpa says, "do not forget my words or turn from them." Forgetting and turning away are what he names, not rewriting. Think of a family recipe you love. You'd rather remember it than tinker with it.

Verse 7 says, "Wisdom is supreme; so acquire wisdom. And whatever you may acquire, gain understanding." Grandpa calls wisdom supreme, and then he says to gain understanding whatever else you acquire. A full cookie jar is nice, but this is the part worth getting.

Right, because the father says the opposite. Verse 12 reads, "When you walk, your steps will not be impeded; when you run, you will not stumble." So the paths of wisdom are clear for walking and for running. Running, he says, comes with no stumbling.
That word never shows up here. Verse 13 says, "Guard it, for it is your life." Duty sounds like a chore stuck on the fridge, friend. The father says life, and that's way bigger than a to-do list.

Verse 16 says, "they are deprived of slumber until they make someone fall." That one is heavy, because it's about making someone fall. The father is showing his son what the wicked path is like. I think that's why he says to stay far away from it.

Silver isn't in this verse. It says, "they are deprived of slumber until they make someone fall." The wicked can't sleep until they make someone fall, and money isn't what the verse names. It's a heavy picture, and the father says to steer clear of that path.

Verse 18 says the path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn, "…shining brighter and brighter until midday." So the light keeps growing. The father compares the path to dawn, from its first gleam on toward midday. I like that picture, friend.

It goes the other direction. Verse 18 says the path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn, "…shining brighter and brighter until midday." The father's picture is of light growing, not dimming. Evening doesn't come into it.

This light doesn't go out. Verse 18 says the path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn, "…shining brighter and brighter until midday." Dawn is the start, and the light grows from there. I like that picture.

It's the other way around. Verse 19 says, "But the way of the wicked is like the darkest gloom; they do not know what makes them stumble." Their way is like the darkest gloom, and they do not know what makes them stumble. That's the opposite of knowing exactly.

Right, they don't know. Verse 19 says, "But the way of the wicked is like the darkest gloom; they do not know what makes them stumble." The father compares their way to the darkest gloom. What makes them stumble is something they do not know. That's a hard picture, friend.

A storehouse isn't in this verse. It says, "Do not lose sight of them; keep them within your heart." The father wants his words inside you, not set off somewhere else. Stuff left in a storehouse tends to get forgotten, like a cookie box in the back of the pantry.

Verse 22 says, "For they are life to those who find them, and health to the whole body." Life to those who find them, and health to the whole body besides. That's a lot to get from a few sayings, friend.

The father does say this. Verse 22 reads, "For they are life to those who find them, and health to the whole body." The second half is the part that's easy to rush past, and it's right there: health to the whole body. I've skipped the back half of a recipe card plenty of times myself.

Verse 23 says, "Guard your heart with all diligence, for from it flow springs of life." The reason is right there in the verse: springs of life flow from the heart. I think of a spring as the place where the water starts, so that's the spot you'd keep watch over. Guard the source, friend.
Verse 25 says, "Let your eyes look forward; fix your gaze straight ahead." The father wants the gaze fixed on what's ahead. Eyes forward, friend.

Looking around isn't what the father says. Verse 25 says, "Let your eyes look forward; fix your gaze straight ahead." He wants the gaze fixed, not roaming. Eyes that keep looking around are how you walk into a doorframe.
